before_times: What is being sold or cleared: the whole home, a few rooms, or single items?
Who has the right to sell: the owner, an executor or administrator, a trustee, an agent under a power of attorney, or a conservator?
Any date the home must be empty by: a closing, a lease end or a listing
Is the home owned, rented or in a building with rules? (a public sale in a rented or condo home needs the building's OK)
after_time: Who will be at the walk-through, and who else has to sign?
Which things stay with the family, and which must not be sold?
Stairs, a gate code, parking and neighbors the crew should know about
Pets in the home, and who looks after them on sale days
secure_page_only: The street address and how to get in (lockbox codes)
Item lists and values, and photos of the contents
The papers that show the right to sell (shown at the walk-through; Rosie keeps only that they were shown)
Anything about the family or the person who owned the home
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult. The agreement is signed only by people with the right to sell (owner, executor or administrator, trustee, financial power-of-attorney agent, conservator) and by every co-owner or co-executor the business asks for. Never a minor.

stop.words: someone is hurt, has fallen or can't breathe
a fire, smoke or a gas smell
stop.says: Leave the home now, and call 911.

go_on.words: a death at home that was never reported, a biohazard, mold, hoarding or an unsafe floor or stairs
go_on.says: Stay out of the area. A cleanup company has to clear it first (no company named). We will not enter until it is cleared.

go_on.words: firearms, medicines or oxygen in the home
go_on.says: Staff never touch them and never sell them. The family removes them before setup.
Staff do not work there until the family says it is safe.

go_on.words: a pet left in the home
go_on.says: A family member must take the pet before setup day.
No sales talk. The walk-through is gentle, and nothing is sold or decided that day.

safety_and_stop_words.business_line: Questions about what an item is worth, what the law says, or what to do with a will go to the business's own line; Rosie gives no value advice

first_steps_and_forms.prep: Before the walk-through: have the papers that show the right to sell, and put aside what stays with the family. Do not throw anything away before the walk-through.

staff.licenses_or_certificates: Each auctioneer holds the license the rules require; no other person license
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs every proposal and any change to the commission
staff.stand_in: The specialist the family asked for is not replaced on silence: a new person is offered only with the family's OK first. An auction stand-in must hold the same license.
staff.roles: Sale specialists (Gil, Irene) run each sale with a crew of 3; appraisers and auctioneers where the rules license them. At the gallery: appraisers Odette and Felix.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult. The agreement is signed only by people with the right to sell (owner, executor or administrator, trustee, financial power-of-attorney agent, conservator) and by every co-owner or co-executor the business asks for. Never a minor.

visit.check_in: The check-in code from whoever meets the specialist at the door; with nobody home on setup and sale days, a start photo and DONE with photos. At the gallery: the code at the desk.
visit.done: Setup ends when the sale is ready. Each sale day ends with DONE. The sale ends with the settlement statement.
visit.changes_at_visit: A new service added later (a cleanout, a buyout, an appraisal of one piece) is priced first and signed first

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: an auctioneer license where the state's rules license auctioneers (each auctioneer, the firm, or both); a bond and a trust account for buyers' money where those rules require them (the business's own bookkeeping); an estate sale firm usually needs only a business registration; a used-goods dealer license, a seller's permit and a per-sale local permit only where the rules require them
license.who: the business, and each auctioneer where the rules license people
ask: An auctioneer license number, for each auctioneer, where the rules require one
A bond and a trust account, where the rules require them
A used-goods dealer license or a seller's permit, only where the rules require one
General liability insurance, and a bond or crime coverage for staff working in clients' homes
license.background: A criminal background check for every person who works in a client's home (the business's own rule)

never_in_a_text: Item lists, item values and the settlement amount: the secure page only
That a home stands empty: told only to the staff on the job
A death, health details or the family's situation: owner and staff texts never say why a home is being sold
